Definition: to dominate, i.e. govern; by implication, to permit
BiblicalUsage: Shalat is power over another, the rule of one man over the life of another. The Preacher saw a time when one man rules over another to his own hurt, and a man to whom God gave riches yet gave no power to eat thereof. The psalm turns the word into a prayer, let not any iniquity have dominion over me, and Esther's story ends with the Jews prevailing over those who sought their hurt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe power over others is the test of a man's heart, because rule without God always ends in hurt. The Preacher saw it, the psalmist prayed against it, and Esther's deliverance shows the other side, that God can turn dominion into rescue. That is why I pray the psalmist's prayer, that no iniquity would have dominion over me.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Queen Esther; King David
